slides.subtitle: What is held, what it costs, its condition and which products come first
slides.title: RMS estate: holdings, costs and first products

scqa: The estate holds 174.8 TiB across databases, the object store and file shares. The object store is 74.8% of that and the file shares 25.0%. The databases hold only 0.3 TiB, so they are not where the cost sits.

The money is a ceiling, not a forecast: up to 1,174.4 USD a month at list prices, mostly from cold object-store buckets. The census key is refused on 90.7% of listed object-store media files, and 40 buckets cannot be listed at all.
What should the owner do first to cut cost, prepare the data and stand up the first products?

First, test archive-tier economics on the 41.9 TiB of cold object-store data and obtain read access to the refused buckets. Next, confirm duplicate candidates by hashing. Then prepare one bounded product, de-identified or aggregated, and remeasure its condition. Rights are settled by the owner's declaration and gate nothing.
slides.title: Savings lie in media stores, not databases, and most media cannot yet be read

terms.meaning: Space that could be removed or stored more cheaply once the check named beside it has been done. It is not space already freed, and it is not a guaranteed saving — the monthly figures are upper bounds at list prices.
Nothing new has been written to that bucket or table for more than a year, judged by the newest write date we could see. It says nothing about whether anyone still reads it — that was not measured.
terms.term: Cold (not written for over a year)

terms.meaning: Two objects whose size and storage fingerprint (ETag) match inside the same store. For large uploads that fingerprint is not a content hash, so a candidate must be confirmed by hashing before any copy is removed.
Database rows that are identical in every measured column. 'Normalised' duplicates also match after trimming spaces and case.
A row whose worst column shows damage: text cut short, a placeholder such as 'N/A' or 'test', an invalid format, stray whitespace or garbled characters.

Blank values in columns whose name or pattern suggests they should always be filled (for example an identifier or a date). The database may not formally require them; the census flags them so an owner can decide.

slides.title: What the terms in this pack mean

terms.meaning: A column that is empty on practically every row: schema carried without data.
A sampled value that looks like an email, phone number, national ID or similar. It is a condition of the data, not a judgement about rights — the owner has declared all rights established.
A cheaper storage tier for data that is kept but rarely opened. Retrieval is slower and carries its own fee, which is why the saving is stated as an upper bound.
Where this pack suggests data should live or how it should be tiered. Every destination here is a proposal for the executive to approve; this pack moved and deleted nothing.
Recorded hours multiplied by the share of two-second windows the admitted music detector did not call music. Silence is set aside first.
The share of labelled windows (or transcript passages) where the model's language label matched the folder the recording was filed under. It is a model reading, not a human verification.

slides.title: What the terms in this pack mean

terms.meaning: Windows where the language model's confidence fell below its threshold, so it gave no language rather than guess.

A calendar date on which a station has at least one news script in the archive, and the distinct hour slots scripted that day. The archive does not carry a script for every hour of every day; the tables show exactly which days and hours it does.
The retained Akki record (census run, GPU job or database reading) that every figure in this pack is traced to. The appendix lists them; the workbook carries the row-level evidence.

The duration written in each file's own header, read with a small ranged request rather than by downloading the file. Every audio file was read this way; for video a sample per folder was read and the rest scaled by that folder's seconds-per-byte, with a stated error.
The range inside which the true figure lies with 95 % confidence, given the files that were read in full. Folders read whole have no interval — they are exact.

The census key can list the bucket but is refused when it tries to read any object. Those files are counted but nothing about their content is estimated. The fix is an access grant on the owner's cloud account, not a change to the census.

slides.title: What the terms in this pack mean

terms.meaning: The cheapest storage tier. Some buckets allow direct reads of Archive objects for a retrieval fee; others answer 'restore required', and a restore must be ordered and paid for before anything can be read.

slides.title: One bucket holds 86.7 TiB of the 130.8 TiB object store

points: The whole estate holds 174.8 TiB across databases, object store and file shares. That is the base for every cost discussion.
The object store holds 130.8 TiB, 74.8% of the estate, in 106 buckets, with 23.0m objects enumerated.
The file shares hold 43.7 TiB, 25.0% of the estate, in 16 shares and 1.5m files.
Databases hold 0.3 TiB, 0.2% of the estate. Database tidying will not move estate economics, though it matters for product quality.
These are measured holdings, not the storage bill. No invoice figure was supplied, so later money figures are list-price estimates.
slides.title: The estate is 174.8 TiB, and the databases are the smallest part of it
What is under review and where it is proposed to go

points: 41.9 TiB across 43 of 106 buckets has not been written for over a year; the table of buckets under review gives each proposed destination.
7.7 TiB, 5.0% of objects, are duplicate candidates, not hash-confirmed; hash before any removal.
40 buckets returned errors when listed; reconcile them with the provider. This differs from buckets that list but refuse reads.
Table bytes are strategy totals, not single-table sizes. Share duplication is unmeasured. Every destination is a proposal.

Which products to stand up first

points: 8 product candidates were scored on readiness, not buyer demand or revenue.
First pilot: reference and master data, then the content catalogue; both need source selection, completeness and freshness checks, and de-duplication.
Third: aggregated channel engagement analytics; de-identify or aggregate first because of personal-data markers.
Rights are settled by the owner's declaration and gate nothing; buyer-side review of fit is still to do.
Staged speech audio is a media-side candidate needing language validation first.
slides.title: Start with reference and catalogue products, then engagement analytics

Commission bounded preparation of one product, using staged audio of 529.5 hours or the first pilot above.
Treat 1,174.4 USD a month as an upper bound; nothing has been moved, deleted or released.
